chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū al-Jārūd, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, from Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī, who said:

I entered upon Fāṭimah عليها السلام, and before her was a tablet in which were the names of the successors from her offspring. I counted twelve; one of them was al-Qāʾim. Three of them were Muḥammad, and four of them were ʿAlī عليه السلام.

key_terms.أَسْمَاءُ الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: The names of the designated successors
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The one who will arise; a title of the Mahdi
key_terms.لَوْحٌ: A tablet or written tablet containing sacred names

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Fāṭimah’s tablet say about the twelve successors and al-Qāʾim?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Jābir ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Anṣārī saw a tablet with Fāṭimah عليها السلام containing the names of the divinely appointed successors from her descendants. It identifies them as twelve in number and includes al-Qāʾim, making the report significant in Shia discussions of the Imams and Imamate.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5408 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Al-Jarud from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) from Jabir ibn Abdullah Al-Ansari, who said:

"I entered upon Sayyida Fatimah {s.a}, and before her {s.a} was a tablet in which were the names of the successors from her offspring. I counted twelve, and one of them was the Riser (Al-Qaʾim (as)). Three of them were named Muhammad (as), and four of them were named Ali (as)."
